math_checks.outcome: I checked the variance of the written assignment a -> Hom(A/a,X). For an arrow a -> a' in A, postcomposition gives A/a -> A/a'; precomposition of functors into X then gives Hom(A/a',X) -> Hom(A/a,X). Postcomposition by X -> Y gives the covariant dependence on X. Thus the written direction Cat -> A-hat is type-consistent under the usual presheaf reading. This is a local variance check, not a verification of the cited p.32 or of any unstated construction.

I compared the displayed source/target with the questioned x -> B/x candidate. If B is the numerator and x ranges over objects of B, that assignment has categorical slices as values and describes a B-to-Cat construction, while the displayed j-family has source Cat and presheaf target. This conditional type mismatch explains why the writer may question the description. The small numerator remains B|A from the ink; I did not use the type check to resolve it or claim the unseen cited text is wrong.
